children: Australia's east‑coast energy market has exceeded expectations in weathering the rise in international gas prices this year, says Commonwealth Bank of Australia's Vivek Dhar. He says batteries, both utility‑scale and behind‑the‑meter, are the key reason. "As impressive as batteries have been in giving the east‑coast energy markets resiliency to international energy prices, the influx of utility‑scale batteries was a market‑driven reaction to low prices in the middle of the day and high evening peak prices," says Dhar. In the medium- to longer-term, the challenge of keeping electricity and gas prices contained remains, he says. That's because of projected annual east‑coast gas shortfalls by 2030, coal power retirements and higher‑than‑expected wind generation costs, among other drivers, says Dhar.
